summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 14.8% QoQ to INR133.3 crore but fell YoY; Q2 order inflow was INR929 crore, with FY27 guidance of 20-25% growth kept.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR133.3 crore in Q2 FY27, up 14.8% QoQ from INR116 crore in Q1, but lower YoY against an exceptionally strong Q2 FY26 execution base. H1 FY27 revenue was INR249.3 crore, PBT INR59 crore and PAT INR44 crore. Q2 fresh orders were INR929 crore (vs INR167 crore a year earlier), taking H1 inflow to INR1,046 crore and closing order book (including negotiated orders) to about INR2,698 crore. Management kept FY27 guidance of 20-25% revenue growth and 35-40% EBITDA margin, expecting H2 to be stronger than H1, and acquired 100% of ST Advanced Composites effective September 17, 2026.

segments.name: Defence electronics (radar, EW, avionics, COMINT/ELINT)
segments.commentary: Order book on hand INR1,742 crore as of call date; INR956 crore negotiated orders awaiting formal receipt, total visibility about INR2,698 crore. International order book INR32 crore as of September 30, 2026.

segments.name: Counter-drone and new products
segments.commentary: Active radars, passive RF detection and jamming in development; management says the product should be ready for demonstration and tenders in 1-2 months. Not part of FY27 projections. Sukhoi-30 self-protection jammer pod is expected to fly in the next few months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% and EBITDA margin of 35-40% maintained.
H2 FY27 expected to be stronger than H1 FY27; business described as Q4-heavy and program-based.
Management said about 50% of the current order book (around INR1,700 crore) needs execution in the next two quarters to meet guidance.
Negotiated orders of about INR900-1,000 crore expected to be contracted in one to two months, with only a small portion executed this year.
Further pipeline of INR1,500-2,000 crore expected before March 2027, not included in negotiated values.
Capex of about INR150 crore over the next two years cited by analyst; management said total investment will be substantially higher and will go to the Board for approval.
International order book expected to grow in FY27.
capex_capacity: About INR150 crore capex over the next two years (figure cited in analyst question); management said total investment will be substantially higher, including a new building and factory already under construction.
Over 1,100 engineers in development and program management; more than 100 engineers in QC.
BrahMos seeker: qualification testing ongoing; production line not yet built, as management is waiting for a production order before investing in the line; some expensive equipment already bought.
Satellite: decision taken to build in-house satellites (100-500 kg class) and payloads, staffing from ex-ISRO scientists; manufacturing infrastructure to follow; details in 6-8 months.
Acquired 100% of ST Advanced Composites Private Limited, effective September 17, 2026, to add advanced composite design and manufacturing.
demand_pricing: Management says there are no ecosystem constraints; AoNs being released every two months, with budgets rising.
Negotiated orders are Central Government tenders with funded programs; delay attributed to internal approval processes, and management said cancellation risk is nil.
Tejas Mk1A contract under negotiation with HAL, expected in the next couple of months; HAL single-vendor and BrahMos seeker orders are in pipeline, not negotiated.
Export: PAR-related radar contracts being pursued, radar front-end orders from Europe expected to execute December to March, and a co-investment in radars with a British company.
Management said the business is shifting toward complete systems and integrated solutions, with competition from multinationals partnering with Indian firms.

qa_highlights.question: Why are negotiated orders (about INR1,000 crore) delayed, and when will they flow into the order book? Is there cancellation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects most to be contracted within one to two months; delay is from internal approval processes. Management said there is no cancellation risk because these are funded Central Government tenders.

qa_highlights.question: With H1 revenue running below the 20-25% guidance, can FY27 guidance be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it never guides quarterly, the business is Q4-heavy and project-based, and production for Q3 and Q4 has started. No change to guidance. Per a later answer, about 50% of the current order book must execute in the next two quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Hawk radar software integration and the Sukhoi-30 pod?
qa_highlights.answer: Hardware for Hawk is ready but software integration has not progressed and is delayed. The Sukhoi-30 self-protection jammer pod is in-house and progressing well, with a flight expected in the next few months. Software-defined radios are being integrated with other platforms in the coming months.

qa_highlights.question: Are you reconsidering space and counter-drone?
qa_highlights.answer: Counter-drone radars, passive RF and jamming are in development; a product demo/tender participation is expected in 1-2 months. The company has decided to build its own satellites, with development in the next 6-8 months and no current contract.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company be able to reach INR2,000 crore of order inflow a year over 3-5 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its aim is much higher numbers and that individual products could each deliver about INR2,000 crore or more. Risks include government-driven procurement, foreign competitors with lower support prices, and win rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Tejas Mk2 delay affect growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tejas Mk2 avionics, cockpit displays and mission computers are the company's scope, and that Tejas Mk1A negotiation is ongoing with HAL. Counter-drone products were not in FY27 projections.

risks_watch: Timing of about INR956 crore negotiated orders and the INR1,500-2,000 crore pipeline before March 2027, which are not yet contracted.
Execution: about 50% of the INR1,700 crore order book needs to execute in the next two quarters to meet guidance; H2 execution is heavily back-loaded.
Hawk radar software integration delay; BrahMos seeker still in qualification with no production order.
Heavy investments in new products, satellites, infrastructure and R&D, much of it expensed through P&L, which may pressure margins.
Tejas Mk2 program delay (undercarriage issues) and the HAL Tejas Mk1A contract timing.
Capex and investment amounts beyond INR150 crore pending Board approval; management said the satellite and product roadmap investment will be significant.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term scale and order visibility, but cautious and somewhat evasive on near-term timing. Management acknowledged that Q2 was muted versus expectations, declined to give quarterly growth guidance, and repeatedly said timelines are outside its control.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR133.3 crore grew 14.8% QoQ but fell YoY against an exceptionally strong Q2 FY26 execution base, and the brief does not give a volume or price split of the growth, so the driver is unclear; the Q2 YoY decline reflects a high base rather than a recurring-business slowdown that is quantified, and the ST Advanced Composites acquisition (effective September 17, 2026) is too recent
